record.context_brief: norm-bounded-below overcomplete operator orbits in Hilbert space
record.original_question: Does there exist a separable Hilbert space H with an overcomplete frame {f_k}_{k=0}^infty whose vectors are uniformly bounded away from zero in norm and for which there is a bounded linear operator T from H to H such that f_k=T^k f_0 for every k>=0? Equivalently, can an overcomplete frame that does not decay in norm still be generated as a one-sided bounded operator orbit?

evidence.quote: Problem 3: Let H denote a separable Hilbert space. Do there exist overcomplete frames for H that are norm-bounded below and have a representation {fk}∞k=0 = {Tkf0}∞k=0 for a bounded operator T : H → H?
Intuitively, Lemma 4.1 says that a frame having the desired type of representation must have “infinite excess in all directions.”

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. A sequence $\{f_k\}_{k=0}^\infty$ of vectors in H is called a frame for H if there exist constants $0 < A \le B < \infty$ such that
$$A\|f\|^2 \;\le\; \sum_{k=0}^\infty |\langle f, f_k\rangle|^2 \;\le\; B\|f\|^2 \qquad \text{for all } f \in H.$$
A frame is called overcomplete if it is not a Riesz basis, equivalently, if there exists at least one index $k_0$ such that $\{f_k\}_{k\ne k_0}$ is still a frame for H. The frame is said to be norm-bounded below if
$$\inf_{k\ge 0} \|f_k\| \;>\; 0.$$
Question: Does there exist a separable Hilbert space H, a vector $f_0 \in H$, and a bounded linear operator $T : H \to H$ such that the orbit
$$\{f_k\}_{k=0}^\infty := \{T^k f_0\}_{k=0}^\infty$$
is an overcomplete frame for H that is norm-bounded below?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent works by Christensen, Hasannasab and collaborators (2018–2020) characterize frames representable as one-sided orbits $\{T^k f_0\}_{k\ge 0}$ of bounded operators, establish strong structural restrictions in the overcomplete case (the image chain of T must have finite length, and finite truncations after the index of stabilization remain frames), and show non-existence for special classes such as Gabor and wavelet frames represented by bounded bijective operators. None of the sources surveyed exhibit an explicit overcomplete, norm-bounded-below example of such an orbit, nor do they prove non-existence in full generality, so the problem appears to remain open.
